# PREVENTION OF PROSTHETIC JOINT INFECTION BEFORE DENTAL PROCEDURES

Prosthetic joints have a small risk (<1 to 5% for the time the prosthesis is in place) of infection from hematogenous seeding. The risk of joint infection after dental or surgical procedures is exceedingly small. Existing data do not support the use of prophylactic antimicrobial prophylaxis for patients with prosthetic joints undergoing procedures. Since the overall risk of prosthesis infection is slightly higher during the first 2 years after implantation, some physicians give prophylactic antimicrobials for patients during the first 2 years after implantation. In addition, antimicrobials are given for theoretical reasons to persons with neutropenia (less than 500 neutrophils and bands per milliliter).
If antimicrobials are given during dental procedures to prevent prosthetic joint infection, give the following:
Preferred
Amoxicillin 2 gm PO 1 hour before procedure ($0.56/day) [R] < OR > Cephalexin 2 gm PO 1 hour before procedure ($0.36/day) [R]
Alternative for patients with penicillin allergy
Clindamycin 600 mg PO 30 minutes before procedure ($1.68/day) [H,O]
